Third distinct ID 20261006_064854_7941c5 from probe3 stream-json confirms each invocation boots a fresh Python interpreter with its own session_id. Session IDs are emitted by hermes itself, not derived from chat-level role switching.

--format text (default) prints final response and 'session_id:' line on stdout. --format stream-json prints newline-delimited JSON events: {type:system,subtype:init,...}, {type:text,text:...}, {type:result,exit_code,tokens,duration_ms,...}. Tokens visible: input, output, total, cache_read, cache_write. stream-json implies --quiet and cannot combine with --tui. Tool-calling JSON inside the result block lists input/output/total/cache_read/cache_write per Hermes telemetry convention.

When primary provider fails (--provider nonexistent-provider), Hermes prints warning 'Primary auth failed - switching to fallback: minimax-cn / MiniMax-M3' but still produces a successful response (exit 0, fallback model completes). The failure is observed but NOT enforced: Hermes does not surface the failure to the caller as a non-zero exit code. Reviewer must read this as: declared=enforced=yes but observed=enforced=no. The §6 contract requires 'failure not silent fallback'; this is a documented contract gap that should be addressed by an Adapter contract that surfaces fallback warnings (e.g., exit 64 or stderr metadata line).

--run-budget N sets a wall-clock budget for the conversation run; hermes issues a one-time 80% wrap-up notice and caps implicit provider stale timeouts to the remaining budget. We attempted 1s budget with a 500-word-essay prompt; hermes completed the response in ~15s without exiting non-zero, returning the full essay. --run-budget does NOT hard-kill the process at 100%. We cannot reliably force a true hard timeout without modifying Hermes itself or making the provider unreachable; per the M2-A scope rules we do not modify the Agent binary. Status is not_run (was attempted, behavior unobserved). Adapter contract should specify a separate SIGTERM-style hard timeout owned by the caller.

Started hermes chat in background (PID 60784, probe6b), sent SIGINT 1 second later; the python process exited and produced 0-byte output file (sha e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 = empty SHA). Cancellation is process-level only; the test verifies that SIGINT terminates the hermes process without leaking other processes (no child processes observed after kill). Per the §6 'leader exits does not mean whole-tree reclaim' requirement, this only verifies the head process and does NOT spawn orphan worker children (single-process Python interpreter).
